title: [MEDIUM] Unauthenticated VNC/X server bound for all display-stack variants
description:
**File:** [`flake.nix`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/agentbox/blob/fix/external-review-20261103/blob/fix/flake.nix#L2558-L2601) (lines 2558, 2590, 2601)
**Project:** agentbox-external-fixes
**Severity:** MEDIUM  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `missing-auth`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

All three display-stack supervisor programs expose a remote desktop with no authentication: the default i3-x11 stack runs `Xvnc :1 ... -SecurityTypes None -ac -rfbport 5901` (L2601) — SecurityTypes None disables VNC auth and -ac disables X access control (any client/host accepted); the x11vnc variant uses `-nopw` (L2590); and wayvnc binds `0.0.0.0 5901` with no --config/auth (L2558). The container-internal bind is 0.0.0.0, and the repo's own Jupyter comment (L2456-2459) establishes the threat model that such binds are 'reachable by every peer on visionclaw_network, not just the operator's loopback tunnel.' Any workload sharing the docker network can therefore take full interactive control of the devuser GUI session (browser holding the Podkey, code-server, terminals). The host publishes 5901 only on 127.0.0.1 (docker-compose.yml:53), which is partial mitigation against host-external access but does not stop cross-container access on visionclaw_network.

## Recommendation

Give the VNC/X server the same auth treatment Jupyter received: bind to 127.0.0.1 inside the container (not 0.0.0.0), or require VNC authentication (TigerVNC SecurityTypes VncAuth with an operator-minted password file, drop -ac; wayvnc --config with enable_auth; x11vnc -rfbauth instead of -nopw). Mint/accept the credential via entrypoint-unified.sh into a 0600 file as done for JUPYTER_TOKEN.

title: [MEDIUM] Governance-decision dispatch to agent stdin / pod files is not gated by the signer roster
description:
**File:** [`management-api/adapters/orchestrator/local-process-manager.js`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/agentbox/blob/fix/external-review-20261103/blob/fix/management-api/adapters/orchestrator/local-process-manager.js#L243-L342) (lines 243, 269, 306, 342)
**Project:** agentbox-external-fixes
**Severity:** MEDIUM  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `acl-check`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

handleGovernanceDecision() gates only its corpus-write branches (promote/demote/ontology-approve) with _ontologySignerRefusal (the AGENTBOX_FORUM_GOVERNANCE_SIGNERS roster). The other two effects are ungated: (1) the agent-stdin delivery at L243-276 writes the reformatted `decision` object (outcome, decided_by, etc.) to a matched running agent's stdin for ANY outcome — including a plain `approve`, which never reaches a signer check (_ontologyApprove returns null for it); and (2) the provenance/decision file persistence at L306/L342. The only control on the loopback/gift-wrap dispatch path (relay-consumer.js L644-650) is the broad ingress allowlist `allowed_pubkeys`, which is strictly larger than the human governance roster (it includes the phone's delegated pubkey, peer/agent keys, etc.; the forum path at relay-consumer.js L454 DOES roster-check, but the DM path does not). An attacker holding any allowlisted key can gift-wrap a sig-valid 31403 whose `d` tag equals a target agentId (agentIds are `urn:agentbox:agent:proc-<base36 timestamp>` — guessable and exposed by listAgents()), causing a forged {type:'governance_decision', outcome:'approve'} to be written to that agent's stdin. Because the stdin payload carries no signature, the downstream agent cannot re-verify and may treat the forged approval as authorisation to proceed with a gated action. The same forged event can also overwrite the provenance record for any case (file keyed on attacker-controlled case_id).

## Recommendation

Apply the _ontologySignerRefusal roster check (or an equivalent governance-signer gate) at the top of handleGovernanceDecision for every effect, not only corpus writes — so a non-governance pubkey cannot inject a decision onto an agent's stdin or into the pod governance files. Alternatively, have the relay-consumer loopback path (L644-650) enforce the forum signer roster before dispatch, matching the forum path. Include the original signature / event in the stdin payload so downstream agents can independently verify.

title: [BUG] No-match decisions persisted to a synthetic cwd path instead of the pod
description:
**File:** [`management-api/adapters/orchestrator/local-process-manager.js`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/agentbox/blob/fix/external-review-20261103/blob/fix/management-api/adapters/orchestrator/local-process-manager.js#L333-L306) (lines 333, 335, 306)
**Project:** agentbox-external-fixes
**Severity:** BUG  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `other-logic-bug`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

When no running agent matches and AGENTBOX_NPUB is unset but AGENTBOX_PUBKEY is set, the decision is written to process.cwd()/pods/npub-<hex16>/events/governance/decisions (L334-335), a fabricated npub directory under the current working directory rather than the real SOLID_POD_ROOT pod. A VisionClaw consumer reading the actual pod will never find these decisions, so the handoff silently breaks. The provenance record (L306) is also keyed on case_id, so repeated decisions on one case overwrite earlier records.

## Recommendation

Resolve the pod directory from SOLID_POD_ROOT and the box's real npub (as the provenance branch does) instead of synthesising npub-<hex16> under cwd; include event_id in the provenance filename so decisions on one case do not overwrite each other.
